themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK versus a 2.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 653% increase (z-score: 6.29)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or enforcement gap on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 16 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (653% spike, z-score: 6.29)
Spike emerged in current reporting period only; no sustained prior trend
Statistically significant anomaly indicating sudden behavior change or enforcement shift
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors flooding high-foot-traffic areas (Madison Ave, Museum Mile)? Interview DSNY and Parks Enforcement.
Has vendor licensing or enforcement changed recently? Check with Department of Health.

themes_detail.label: Trash Infrastructure Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Three interconnected waste complaints surged THIS WEEK and LAST WEEK: dumpster complaints up 967% (4 vs. 0.4 avg), litter basket complaints up 700% (4 vs. 0.5 avg), and commercial disposal complaints up 567% (5 vs. 0.8 avg)—suggesting systemic sanitation infrastructure failure.
evidence: Dumpster complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Litter basket complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Commercial disposal complaints: 5 last week vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)
Litter basket requests also spiked to 10 (567% over baseline, z-score: 12.02)—indicating both capacity shortage and resident demand
reporting_angles: Is there a collection schedule disruption? Contact DSNY about missed pickups or equipment failures on UES.
Interview residents and commercial tenants on Madison Ave and side streets about overflow trash and pest attraction.

themes_detail.label: Boiler/Heat System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK versus a 0.8 weekly average—a 300% spike (z-score: 5.2)—coming just as heating season approaches, signaling potential winter hardship for tenants.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score: 5.2)
Heat/hot water remains a top category overall (810 complaints in 90-day window), but spike indicates recent acceleration
Timing coincides with seasonal heating system activation and tenant preparation
reporting_angles: Interview tenants in buildings with reported boiler issues; verify repair timelines and landlord responsiveness.
Check DOB permits: 1,765 alteration filings in 90 days—are older buildings deferred necessary HVAC maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Day Care Facility Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Day care complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.5 weekly average—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—a small but statistically significant emerging issue in a residential district.
evidence: 3 day care complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
No prior trend; spike is isolated to current reporting period
Day care is infrastructure-critical for UES working families; complaints may signal licensing, safety, or overcrowding issues
reporting_angles: What type of complaints? Check Department of Health and NYC Department of Children's Services for recent violations.
Interview parents and providers about staffing, capacity, or facility concerns.

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Enforcement Gap
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting a sudden decline in off-leash enforcement in parks and residential areas.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Isolated spike with no sustained trend history
Could reflect seasonal behavior change (fall weather increasing park use) or Parks enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Enforcement about recent staffing or policy changes affecting off-leash patrol.
Canvass Central Park and neighborhood parks for resident safety concerns.
